blocks.html: A condition in which the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormone. The thyroid hormone runs the body’s metabolism so people who have hypothyroidism typically experience issues with their metabolism.

blocks.text: Common Supplements Found in Our Pharmacy to Help Combat Symptoms

blocks.html: Iodine is the most crucial element you need in order to treat hypothyroidism because it makes up the structure of both thyroid hormones T3 and T4. Without iodine, you would not be able to produce optimal amounts of either hormone.
Vitamin B12 This water-soluble vitamin is essential for proper cell metabolism and is also responsible for nerve cell function and reducing brain fog.

Selenium The body needs selenium for building the enzymes that convert T4 into T3, which are thyroid hormones. T3 is the more active thyroid hormone of the two. Selenium also helps reduce inflammation and helps remove substances which may harm the thyroid.
Magnesium Magnesium converts T4 into T3 and also helps to boost T4 production.

Zinc can be helpful by allowing the T3 receptors in your cells to bind to T3 when it arrives. Without it, you wouldn’t be able to absorb the T3 generated by your diet or medications. It is also necessary for many biological functions which include producing testosterone, healing wounds, boosting immunity.

During early stages, you may not develop any symptoms. As the disease progresses, you may notice: fatigue, weight gain, mood swings, lethargy, feeling cold, hair loss or dryness, brittle nails, constipation, dry skin, enlarged thyroid, high cholesterol, sexual dysfunction, sluggishness.

Your doctor might prescribe a synthetic thyroid hormone to help control your hypothyroidism. This medication is oral and will help restore adequate hormone levels to reverse the signs and symptoms of hypothyroidism. Most patients report feeling much better as soon as starting treatment. The medication can also help gradually lower cholesterol levels elevated by the disease and may also reverse any weight gain. Treatment for hypothyroidism is often lifelong, but it is important to check your thyroid hormone levels to maintain a proper balance and determine if the medication is working properly.

It may take some time to fine tune the right dosage for your body so your doctor may order lab tests more frequently initially after treatment has started. In addition, if you have too much hormone introduced to your body, you my experience the following side effects:

items: Increased appetite
Insomnia
Heart Palpitations
Shakiness

blocks.html: There are is no way to prevent hypothyroidism, but there are various ways to help prevent hypothyroidism from becoming a serious condition as well as lowering the risk of developing hypothyroidism if you follow the following guidelines:

items: Protect yourself against x-rays and ask for a shield when appropriate.
Avoid smoking
Avoid starvation diets
Check your lab work annually
